text:
Peak shaving with increased self-consumption (multiuse)
In projects with self-consumption and in energy system projects, the "multiuse" function can be used to optimize the inverter behavior for power exchange at the grid point of interconnection. In the process the "peak shaving" function and increased self-consumption are combined to further reduce the energy costs.
The "multi-use" function divides the useful range of the battery area of use into 2 sections:
Section below the SOC limiting value
If the battery state of charge is below the limiting value, the battery is used for peak shaving.
To do this, the battery-storage system is discharged in this range if the grid-supplied power exceeds the specified grid-supply limit. The battery is charged from the utility grid or with surplus PV energy if the feed-in power is higher than the specified feed-in limit.
If the battery is charged with energy drawn from the utility grid, a negative value must be entered for the load limit.
Example: If the peak load must be limited above 50 kW and the battery must be charged below 50 kW, 50 kW must be entered as the grid-supply limit and -50 kW as the load limit.
Section above the SOC limiting value
If the state of charge of the battery is above the limiting value, self-consumption must preferably be optimized.
To do so, the battery-storage system is discharged in this range to limit the utility grid-supplied power to the specified maximum value. As a rule, this is 0 kW. The battery is typically charged using excess PV energy. In the case of increased self-consumption, the battery-storage system can be discharged up to the specified SOC limiting value. If the battery is not charged with energy drawn from the utility grid, 0 kW must be entered for the feed-in limit.

The "multi-use" function divides the useful range of the battery area of use into 2 sections:

metadata.title: Requirements on your own consumption data

text:
Requirements on your own consumption data
If you want to import your own consumption data for the load profile, the data must meet the following requirements:
The data series begins on January 1 at 00:00 a.m.
The values cover a complete year (365 days or a leap year with 366 days) or an entire week (7 days). If the values cover 7 days, a complete year is created from this data.
The values have a time interval of 5, 10, 15, 30 or 60 minutes.
The power or energy values are positive and indicated in the following units: W, kW, Wh or kWh.
All values are in the first column.
Either a period (.) or a comma (,) is used as decimal separator.
The data is in CSV format (.csv).
markdown:
# Requirements on your own consumption data

If you want to import your own consumption data for the load profile, the data must meet the following requirements:

*   The data series begins on January 1 at 00:00 a.m.
    
*   The values cover a complete year (365 days or a leap year with 366 days) or an entire week (7 days). If the values cover 7 days, a complete year is created from this data.
    
*   The values have a time interval of 5, 10, 15, 30 or 60 minutes.
    
*   The power or energy values are positive and indicated in the following units: W, kW, Wh or kWh.
    
*   All values are in the first column.
    
*   Either a period (.) or a comma (,) is used as decimal separator.
    
*   The data is in CSV format (.csv).

text:
Configuring the battery system
Prerequisite:
You must have opened an energy system project and planned it up to the project page Energy system.
Procedure:
In the central workspace, click on the button [Battery system].
The Battery system quick configuration dialog box will open.
If the project is to be designed without battery system, disable the checkbox Take battery-storage system into account and click on [Apply changes].
To make a quick configuration, make the required settings in the tab Technical configuration.
or
To configure detailed settings, Click on the button [To the detailed configuration] and make the required settings in the tab Technical configuration.
Make the desired settings in the tabs Battery inverter, Financing and Tariffs.
If you designed the battery system in the quick configuration view, click on [Apply changes].
If you designed the battery system in the detailed configuration view, click on the button [Energy system] in the tab Technical configuration in the area Next steps.
markdown:
# Configuring the battery system

**Prerequisite:**

*   You must have opened an energy system project and planned it up to the project page **Energy system**.
    

**Procedure:**

1.  In the central workspace, click on the button **\[Battery system\]**.
2.  The **Battery system quick configuration** dialog box will open.
3.  If the project is to be designed without battery system, disable the checkbox **Take battery-storage system into account** and click on **\[Apply changes\]**.
4.  To make a quick configuration, make the required settings in the tab **Technical configuration**.  
    **or**  
    To configure detailed settings, Click on the button **\[To the detailed configuration\]** and make the required settings in the tab **Technical configuration**.
5.  Make the desired settings in the tabs **Battery inverter**, **Financing** and **Tariffs**.
6.  If you designed the battery system in the quick configuration view, click on **\[Apply changes\]**.
7.  If you designed the battery system in the detailed configuration view, click on the button **\[Energy system\]** in the tab **Technical configuration** in the area **Next steps**.

text:
Planning the Energy Management
Prerequisite:
You must have opened an energy system project and planned it up to the project page Energy system.
Procedure:
Click on the [Energy management] button in the central workspace.
The page Planning the energy management will open.
Make the required settings.
In the area Next steps, click on the button [Energy system].
markdown:
# Planning the Energy Management

**Prerequisite:**

*   You must have opened an energy system project and planned it up to the project page **Energy system**.
    

**Procedure:**

1.  Click on the **\[Energy management\]** button in the central workspace.
2.  The page **Planning the energy management** will open.
3.  Make the required settings.
4.  In the area **Next steps**, click on the button **\[Energy system\]**.

text:
Calculating automatic design suggestions
Prerequisite:
You must have opened a project and planned it up to the project page Configure PV system.
Procedure:
In the area Inverter design, click on the button [Automatic design].
The Design dialog box will open.
Make the desired settings.
Click on [OK].
The proposed inverters are added and displayed in the area PV inverter.
To generate a system proposal for off-grid systems, click on [System assistant].
markdown:
# Calculating automatic design suggestions

**Prerequisite:**

*   You must have opened a project and planned it up to the project page **Configure PV system**.
    

**Procedure:**

1.  In the area **Inverter design**, click on the button **\[Automatic design\]**.
2.  The **Design** dialog box will open.
3.  Make the desired settings.
4.  Click on **\[OK\]**.
5.  The proposed inverters are added and displayed in the area **PV inverter**.
6.  To generate a system proposal for off-grid systems, click on **\[System assistant\]**.
